## Overview

::: {.intro}
Geostatistical models are increasingly important in public health
research due to the rise in spatial health data. This intensive course
suits statisticians and public health professionals wanting to enhance
their skills in geospatial analysis and modelling. Participants learn
about spatial data structures and geostatistics through real-life
examples, progressing from basic to complex models using Bayesian
inference with the INLA approach.

The focus is on spatial patterns of malaria and other health outcomes,
with an emphasis on skills that continue to develop after the course.
:::

## Who Should Apply

This course is designed for statisticians and public health
professionals who want to build their geospatial analysis and
modelling skills. Candidates should have:

- Basic experience with R
- An understanding of statistical inference
- Introductory knowledge of Bayesian statistical methods

## What You'll Learn

Participants learn Bayesian geostatistical modelling approaches — such
as INLA and INLAbru — applied to real malaria and public health data.
The exact tools and special topics (e.g. spatial disaggregation) vary
by cohort; see this year's [Edition page](../editions/index.qmd) for
the current curriculum.

Lecture topics include:

- Introduction to Geostatistics
- Spatial Data in R
- Areal Data and Models
- Geostatistical Models in INLA
- Basics of Point Process Models
